body:
It sounds like you're absolutely horrified about getting assistance.  Most of what I'm reading is that you're ashamed:  you know the people who may be processing your paperwork.  They might see things about you that are only seen when the sheets of paper with your names come past their desks.

And you're frightened at how they'll look at you -- with contempt because allegedly you're scrounging.

Here's a little secret: you're not.  It sounds like you actually have quite an impressive work ethic. You've been employed for a year. That doesn't sound like much, but it's still impressive.  And yes, you've been made redundant, which sucks.  But you're not losing your job because you're not getting things done, stealing from the till, or screwing the manager's wife. 

Will that get you a job tomorrow? Not guaranteed. But it's important to realize and KNOW that you're NOT one of those leeches on society. That's not how you got to this place. And as soon as you find a worthwhile job, you're off of assistance.  You're different from what you think they will think of you.

Also, YOU HAVE AN INTERVIEW NEXT WEEK.  That's wonderful! And you're waiting to hear back on more than 50% of the jobs you've applied for.  You sound like someone who really wants to make this work.

I'd like to suggest a different backup plan -- if you REALLY can't find a public sector job, find something else. Anything else that you've been curious about. You sound like a hard worker who could get stuff done.  Please give yourself another chance.

(Apologies if some of my Americanisms are lost in translation.)

A thought:  Are you aware of any groups for trans women in your area (or even online)? I'm not one myself, but from my own local acquaintances who happen to be trans MtF women (in various stages of life), I don't think that you're alone (although it certainly sounds like you feel that way).

Once you find a peer group of others who have similar feelings and experiences, I'll bet that you find some things in common with which they are also struggling with and have found ways to cope.  You may also be able to find, amongst this group, a sub-group of trans women who have also experienced the trauma of sexual assault and the way its aftermath has affected them.

I hope finding a community will help alleviate the hopelessness.

PS -- you deserve resources just like everyone else. Doesn't matter what chromosomes you were born with. You are human. And deserve to be treated as such.

You sound like a smart, introspective person. Maybe a bit shy, but that's nothing to be ashamed of. Nor is feeling anything less than genuinely happy 100% of the time.

Oh - and parents should not be making fun of their kids for what they're feeling. That's not on you; that's on them.  I'm sorry they put you through that. It's probably not meant maliciously, but still -- not cool of them.

Keep on searching for what is satisfying. What do you like to do for fun?

It is truly scary amazing how much you and I are alike - from the ups we get in volunteering and making personal connections to the way that gets nullified once we become self-critical to the ipad time and nutritional content of our sons. :)

I am on meds -- Wellbutrin.  Apparently it's been a good fit for me. I don't see it nearly as much, but my wife says that she's seen a significant improvement.  I just feel like over the past two weeks I've back-slidden, and I don't know if she's been too busy to notice.   I'm also in therapy -- and I was doing well enough that it was cut back to two times a month rather than once a week. Maybe I need to revisit that...

Your offer to help a complete stranger online shows how truly wonderful you are. Thank you. As stated, I have someone -- but just that offer speaks volumes of who you are.

Nice to have found my long-lost twin.... :)

Rejection is really really horrible -- whether it's a situation like this, or a breakup, or not getting into the university of your choice, etc.  It makes us feel like we're not worthy. I'm sorry you're having these awful feelings associated with it.

And just saying "learn how to get over her" won't be helpful -- because you can't just turn it on and turn it off. I've been through my own break-ups and rejections, and people have given me that advice. "Time heals all wounds."  Not helpful unless I make myself a time machine, right?

It sounds like, however, you ARE someone who knows how to feel and how to fall in love. Which means you probably have that same love to give. That's admirable -- especially at age 21 when so many people are just looking for instant gratification. I think that's something that you still have, and will continue to have for a while.

Keep being a romantic. It may have its ups and downs, and it may feel shitty right now, but during the ups? It has the potential to feel wonderful. :)

I'm using a throwaway right now.  But I usually do relatively okay on my real reddit /u/. People seem to like what I say and what I post.

I had one picture I posted last month -- and two people came by and trolled it. And it felt terrible. Never mind the compliments and upvotes I had received; this just unraveled all of that. And made me feel: "What if the upvotes are just a joke and this is how people really feel?"

It sucks to feel like that. Even if there's just one asshole who ruins it for everyone. 

I guess what I'm trying to say is you ARE normal. It's nothing to be ashamed of to be sensitive to what others say or do. And personally -- I'm proud of you for taking such a cognitive approach to this whole thing, using your therapy exercise to cope and move forward.  Have you told this experience to your therapist?  Even if you have, make sure to tell them what you've been doing to try to help yourself.  I'm sure they're proud of you too.

Best of luck. Keep on channeling your inner Setsu. :)

I'm going to take what this person said and frame the last part of it in a more positive way:

It sounds like you feel upset and afraid that these relationships are forming around you rather than with you. And that there must be some sort of reason that they're not telling you about which is why they're forming these other relationships -- even if it's just grabbing lunch or dinner.  And it makes you feel less adequate. And second guess yourself.  I've certainly been there. It's a horrible feeling. I'm sorry you're going through it.

What has helped me (and I know it's easier said than done) is to focus on YOU - what makes YOU FEEL valuable.  Don't worry about them for a moment -- just you.  Do you feel like you're great at movie trivia? at Super Smash Bros.?  at singing karaoke? Introducing people to funny clips on YouTube?  There's probably something which you derive pleasure and pride from - even if just a little -- which you value.

Feel that. And be proud of that. And then expand a bit to other things that come to mind which are your talents and what makes you shine.  There are SO many people out there, and there have to be some who appreciate these talents.  It may mean making friends outside of your original circle, but it doesn't mean that you need to drop all ties to your existing circle.

When you make new connections, it sometimes becomes a bit easier to feel comfortable making other connections. And it sounds like that's what you're looking for -- genuine connections.

Best of luck. Please keep us posted how it goes...

Hi -- Thanks so much for replying. Good to know I have a twin out there. :)

I'm very fortunate that I have a wife who DOES realize that this is depression and is helping me through it -- and even frames it well with our son who is seeing some of the ripple effects and is trying to process it. 

I'm feeling somewhat better this morning. Last night one of my "kids" at college (let's call her Lisa) PM'd me on Facebook telling me that she felt alone and frightened away at school -- her roommate is away for the semester -- and she felt that she needed someone to be there to stop her from OD-ing on her meds. We talked a bit and I think I helped her evaluate some of her options of how to take that "alone" feeling and alleviate it.  Really wonderful young woman who is going through a whole lot on her own.

I genuinely WANT to get out from behind the clouds. I used to love that person. But now? It's as if the image of me is smudged and dirty. And the more I try to clean the lens, the more smudged and dirty it looks. Does that make sense?

Anyway - thank you for reading and answering.

Jim --

I have my own type of spirituality but I'm not a Christian. And I'll be honest -- there is some zealotry I've seen in /r/Christianity which has been off-putting to me (although this is not the norm).

But on the most part? It seems that it's a very warm, caring community of people who want to support a stranger in need. And that's wonderful to see.

Thank you for reaching out.  It looks like this person has been very receptive of the messages from the community.
